Members of the dog family.Wolf: Wolves are the ancestors of all domestic dogs, and a pack's howl can carry for several kilometres.
Members of the dog family.Fox: Foxes can hear a watch ticking from 40 metres away and may use Earth's magnetic field to aim their pounce.
Members of the dog family.Coyote: Coyotes have spread across North America, even into big cities like Chicago and New York, despite centuries of hunting.
Members of the dog family.Jackal: Golden jackals are surprisingly adaptable, and mated pairs often hunt together and may stay together for life.
Members of the dog family.Dingo: Dingoes arrived in Australia thousands of years ago, probably with seafaring people, and became the continent's top predator.
Members of the dog family.Fennec fox: The fennec fox's huge ears, up to about 15 cm long, shed heat and let it listen for insects moving under desert sand.
Members of the dog family.Dhole: The dhole is an Asian wild dog that whistles to keep its pack together, and it can take down prey much larger than itself.
Members of the dog family.African wild dog: African wild dogs, also called painted dogs, have unique coat patterns and hunt with one of the highest success rates among predators.
Members of the dog family.Maned wolf: Despite the name, the maned wolf is not a wolf or a fox; it's a unique long-legged canid that stalks South American grasslands.
Members of the dog family.Raccoon dog: This fox-like canid from East Asia is the only dog-family member that hibernates in winter.
Members of the dog family.Arctic fox: Arctic foxes change from white to brown with the seasons and can survive temperatures below minus 50 degrees Celsius.
Members of the dog family.Hyena: Hyenas look like dogs, but they are closer to cats and mongooses, and spotted hyena females dominate the clan.
Members of the dog family.Aardwolf: The aardwolf is a type of hyena, not a canine, and it eats thousands of termites in a single night.
Members of the dog family.Thylacine: The thylacine, or Tasmanian tiger, was a dog-like marsupial; its resemblance to dogs is a case of convergent evolution.
Members of the dog family.Red panda: Red pandas are not dogs, bears or true pandas; they sit in a family of their own, famously fond of bamboo.
Members of the dog family.Raccoon: Raccoons are in their own family, Procyonidae; the dog-like face and 'mask' are a coincidence of looks, not relation.
Members of the dog family.Badger: Badgers are mustelids, relatives of weasels and otters, not dogs, and they dig huge underground setts that may last generations.
Members of the dog family.Wolverine: The wolverine is a stocky member of the weasel family, not a dog, though it has a reputation for fearlessly attacking larger prey.
Members of the dog family.Mongoose: Mongooses belong to their own family, close to hyenas and cats, and are famous for taking on venomous snakes.
Members of the dog family.Meerkat: Meerkats are small mongooses, not dogs, and their group members take turns watching for hawks from lookout posts.
Members of the dog family.Seal: Seals are caniforms, so they're distant cousins of dogs, but they form their own family and spend most of life at sea.
Members of the dog family.Prairie dog: Prairie dogs are rodents, not dogs; they're named for their warning bark, and their towns can hold thousands of burrows.
Members of the dog family.Sea lion: Sea lions are eared seals, not dogs; unlike true seals they can rotate their hind flippers forward and walk on land.
Members of the dog family.Bear: Bears are a separate family, the Ursidae; they share a distant ancestor with dogs, but are not canids.

Tropical fruits.Mango: India's national fruit, and a drupe with a big pit, it is one of the most eaten fruits worldwide.
Tropical fruits.Pineapple: It contains bromelain, an enzyme that digests protein, so it can make your tongue tingle.
Tropical fruits.Papaya: It's the source of papain, which is used as a meat tenderizer.
Tropical fruits.Banana: Bananas are berries botanically, and the Cavendish is a clone, so a fungus threatens it.
Tropical fruits.Guava: Its vitamin C content can beat oranges by several times, in a sweet pink fruit.
Tropical fruits.Passion fruit: Missionaries named it for the Passion of Christ, since its flower seemed to reflect it.
Tropical fruits.Rambutan: The name comes from the Malay word for 'hairy', due to its spiky red shell.
Tropical fruits.Durian: It's so smelly that it is banned from many hotels and public transit in Singapore.
Tropical fruits.Jackfruit: The biggest tree-borne fruit in the world, which can weigh dozens of pounds.
Tropical fruits.Dragon fruit: It grows on a night-blooming cactus, and the white flesh is covered in black seeds.
Tropical fruits.Mangosteen: Nicknamed 'queen of fruits', it has a purple rind and creamy white segments.
Tropical fruits.Star fruit: Also known as carambola, it makes star shapes when sliced, and is harmful to kidney patients.
Tropical fruits.Coconut: Botanically a drupe, not a nut, and also the one seed that can float across oceans.
Tropical fruits.Apple: Temperate fruit, an apple tree needs cold winters to flower, which is why apples fail in the true tropics.
Tropical fruits.Pear: A cool-climate pome that grows on trees in orchards, with China making most of the world's supply.
Tropical fruits.Cherry: A temperate stone fruit that needs winter chill to bloom, so it's not tropical.
Tropical fruits.Plum: It's grown in orchards from Europe to the US and needs cold winter chill, so it's not tropical.
Tropical fruits.Apricot: Apricots grow in dry, temperate climates, and kernels inside the stones are toxic, so it's not tropical.
Tropical fruits.Gooseberry: A cool-climate berry that grows in Britain and northern Europe.
Tropical fruits.Rhubarb: Only the stalks are eaten, as the leaves are toxic, and it's a cool-season crop; botanically a vegetable.
Tropical fruits.Cranberry: It grows in bogs in cool climates, and the berries are harvested by flooding the fields.
Tropical fruits.Quince: A temperate pome that is ancient and fragrant, and needs cooking to soften.
Tropical fruits.Blackcurrant: A cool-climate berry rich in vitamin C, and they are the base of cassis liqueur.
Tropical fruits.Raspberry: A temperate berry that grows in cool regions, and botanically an aggregate fruit.

Things made from wheat.Couscous: Tiny steamed pellets of semolina, traditionally rolled by hand. It is a staple across North Africa, not a grain in its own right.
Things made from wheat.Bulgur: Wheat that is parboiled, dried and cracked, so it only needs soaking. It is the base of tabbouleh and kibbeh.
Things made from wheat.Semolina: Coarse flour milled from hard durum wheat. Its high protein gives dried pasta its firm bite and golden color.
Things made from wheat.Seitan: Made by washing dough until only wheat gluten remains. Buddhist monks in China have used it as a meat stand-in for centuries.
Things made from wheat.Orzo: Pasta shaped like rice, and its Italian name means barley. It is made from durum wheat semolina.
Things made from wheat.Udon: Thick Japanese noodles of wheat flour, water and salt. Good ones are kneaded by foot in traditional shops.
Things made from wheat.Naan: Leavened wheat flatbread slapped onto the wall of a clay tandoor oven. The blistered bubbles come from that fierce heat.
Things made from wheat.Croissant: Layers of wheat dough folded with butter dozens of times. It descends from the Austrian kipferl, not a French invention.
Things made from wheat.Pita: Wheat bread that puffs into a hollow pocket in a very hot oven, as steam inflates the dough from inside.
Things made from wheat.Pretzel: A wheat dough dipped in lye or baking soda solution before baking, which gives the dark, glossy crust and its distinctive tang.
Things made from wheat.Cream of Wheat: A hot cereal of farina, the milled middlings of wheat. It was first made in 1893 in North Dakota.
Things made from wheat.Polenta: Boiled cornmeal, not wheat. In northern Italy it was the everyday staple before pasta and wheat bread became widespread.
Things made from wheat.Grits: Ground corn, often hominy, simmered into porridge. Its name comes from an Old English word for coarse meal.
Things made from wheat.Quinoa: A seed, not a grain, from a plant related to spinach. It is naturally gluten-free and contains all nine essential amino acids.
Things made from wheat.Tapioca: Starch from the cassava root, so no wheat at all. Cassava must be processed to remove natural cyanide-producing compounds.
Things made from wheat.Rice noodles: Made from rice flour and water, which is why they suit gluten-free diets. Pad thai and pho both rely on them.
Things made from wheat.Mochi: Pounded sticky rice, which makes it chewy rather than bready. In Japan, choking on mochi sadly sends people to hospital each New Year.
Things made from wheat.Arepa: A griddled cake of pre-cooked cornmeal, beloved in Venezuela and Colombia. It is naturally free of wheat.
Things made from wheat.Popcorn: A special corn variety whose hard shell traps moisture, which turns to steam and bursts the kernel open at roughly 180 C.
Things made from wheat.Oatmeal: Made from oats, a different cereal from wheat. Oats are often processed near wheat, so celiacs need certified gluten-free ones.
Things made from wheat.Congee: A rice porridge eaten across Asia, often for breakfast or when ill. Cooked long enough, rice breaks down into a creamy gruel.
Things made from wheat.Corn tortilla: Made from corn treated with lime in a process called nixtamalization, which boosts nutrition. Flour tortillas are the wheat version.
Things made from wheat.Kasha: Roasted buckwheat groats. Despite the name, buckwheat is no wheat at all, but a seed related to rhubarb, so it is gluten-free.
Things made from wheat.Rice paper: The Vietnamese wrapper is rice flour and water. Spring rolls are sold dry in sheets and softened in water before filling.

Foods that don't contain what their name.Egg cream: A New York classic of milk, seltzer and chocolate syrup. It has neither egg nor cream, and nobody knows why it got the name.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Bombay duck: It is not duck at all but bummalo, a lizardfish from Mumbai coast, usually eaten dried and fried.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Welsh rarebit: Cheese sauce on toast, with no rabbit anywhere. The older name Welsh rabbit was a joke on the Welsh being poor.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Hot dog: There is no dog. The name was likely a joke from the 1900s about sausages of dubious contents, popularized by sports cartoons.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Buffalo wings: They are chicken wings, and they come from Buffalo, New York, not from buffalo. They were reportedly first served at the Anchor Bar in 1964.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Head cheese: A cold cut of jellied meat from a pig or calf's head, with no cheese. The word cheese here meant something molded.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Grape-Nuts: The cereal contains neither grapes nor nuts. It is made of wheat and barley, and its inventor believed that glucose was called grape sugar.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Cream of tartar: A white powder, potassium bitartrate, that settles in wine barrels. It is neither cream nor tartar, and stabilizes egg whites.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Toad in the hole: Sausages baked in Yorkshire pudding batter. No toads are involved, it's just a quirky British name.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Ladyfingers: Light sponge biscuits used in tiramisu. They are not fingers, though a few are shaped like them.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Duck sauce: Sweet plum or apricot dip served with Chinese takeaway in America. It contains no duck.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Chicken fried steak: It's beef steak, breaded and fried like chicken. A Texas classic with white gravy.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Jelly bean: Hard sugar shell with a soft center, and no actual jelly. Reagan kept a jar on his desk as president.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Sweetbreads: Neither sweet nor bread: they are the thymus or pancreas of a calf or lamb. They are prized in French cooking.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Buffalo mozzarella: Truly made from the milk of water buffalo, an animal that farms in Campania. So it fits its name.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Bird's nest soup: Made from real nests of swiftlets, built from the birds' hardened saliva. It is one of the world's priciest foods.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Oyster sauce: It really contains oyster extract, cooked down from oysters and discovered by accident in 1888, according to the legend.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Fish sauce: Genuinely fish, usually anchovies, fermented with salt for a year or more. It's a savory staple of Southeast Asia.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Crab cake: Truly made of crab meat, bound with a bit of breadcrumbs and egg. Maryland is famous for it.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Cheesecake: It does contain cheese, usually soft cheese like cream cheese or ricotta. The ancient Greeks served it at the Olympics.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Peanut butter: Ground peanuts, so it is honest. Peanuts are actually legumes, not nuts.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Chicken nugget: It really is chicken, usually, though it is processed. They were invented in the 1950s at Cornell University by Robert Baker.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Lobster roll: Real lobster meat in a bun. It is a New England summer must, and it can be served hot with butter or cold with mayonnaise.
Foods that don't contain what their name.Beef Wellington: It really is beef, wrapped in pastry. Whether named after the Duke of Wellington is guesswork, as the dish may only resemble his boot.

Countries on the Danube.Germany: The Danube rises here in the Black Forest, where the Brigach and Breg streams meet, and the river begins its 2,850 km run.
Countries on the Danube.Austria: The Danube flows through Vienna, and the waltz The Blue Danube by Johann Strauss II became an unofficial anthem for the country.
Countries on the Danube.Slovakia: Bratislava is one of four capitals on the Danube, along with Vienna, Budapest and Belgrade, and it sits next to two borders.
Countries on the Danube.Hungary: The river splits Budapest into hilly Buda and flat Pest, and a famous chain bridge joined them in 1849.
Countries on the Danube.Croatia: The Danube forms much of its eastern border with Serbia, and the city of Vukovar was devastated in 1991.
Countries on the Danube.Serbia: Belgrade stands where the Sava meets the Danube, a strategic spot fought over for centuries.
Countries on the Danube.Romania: The river's Delta, a UNESCO site in Romania, is Europe's best-preserved delta and home to pelicans.
Countries on the Danube.Bulgaria: The Danube forms most of its northern border with Romania, and its Black Sea port is not on the river.
Countries on the Danube.Ukraine: The river reaches the Black Sea through a delta shared by Romania and Ukraine, where Ukraine holds the northern channels.
Countries on the Danube.Czech Republic: It has the Vltava and Elbe rivers, and none of the Danube flows through it, despite its closeness.
Countries on the Danube.Poland: Its main rivers are the Vistula and Oder flowing north to the Baltic, not toward the Danube.
Countries on the Danube.Switzerland: Swiss rivers feed the Rhine and Rhône, though a small part of the Inn river that joins the Danube starts there.
Countries on the Danube.Slovenia: Its rivers, like the Sava, eventually reach the Danube, but the Danube itself doesn't pass through.
Countries on the Danube.Bosnia: Bosnia's rivers reach the Danube through the Sava, but none of the Danube passes through its land.
Countries on the Danube.Italy: The Po flows across northern Italy to the Adriatic, and the Danube does not reach it.
Countries on the Danube.Greece: Greece lies in the south Balkans, and its rivers drain to the Aegean rather than the Danube.
Countries on the Danube.Turkey: Only a sliver of Turkey is in Europe, and the Danube doesn't reach it.
Countries on the Danube.Belarus: Belarus sits on the Dnieper and Neman basins, and the Danube doesn't flow there.
Countries on the Danube.Montenegro: Its rivers flow to the Adriatic or to the Danube basin through tributaries, but not the river itself.
Countries on the Danube.North Macedonia: The Vardar river runs from here to the Aegean, not to the Danube.
Countries on the Danube.France: France gets the Rhine, Loire, Seine and Rhône, though the Danube never touches it.
Countries on the Danube.Albania: Its rivers run to the Adriatic, away from the Danube.
Countries on the Danube.Lithuania: Lithuania lies on the Baltic Sea side, where the Neman river drains.
Countries on the Danube.Netherlands: The Rhine, not the Danube, reaches the sea in the Netherlands, and the two rivers' basins are linked only by the old Rhine-Main-Danube canal.

Elements that are gases at room temperat.Hydrogen: Hydrogen is the lightest element and makes up roughly three-quarters of the universe's normal matter by mass.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Helium: Helium was detected on the Sun in 1868, before anyone found it on Earth; its name comes from the Greek sun god, Helios.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Nitrogen: Nitrogen makes up about 78 percent of the air you breathe, and is a gas that's inert enough to keep chip bags from going stale.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Oxygen: Oxygen is about 21 percent of air, a level that arose when cyanobacteria began photosynthesizing billions of years ago.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Fluorine: Fluorine is the most reactive element, a pale yellow gas that can make even glass burn.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Neon: Neon glows red-orange when electrified, and signs of other colors use different gases or coatings.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Chlorine: Chlorine is a greenish-yellow gas used as a weapon in World War I and today to disinfect pools and water.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Argon: Argon makes up almost 1 percent of air, and its name comes from the Greek for 'lazy' because it hardly reacts.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Krypton: Krypton's name means 'hidden', and from 1960 to 1983 the meter was defined using its light.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Xenon: Xenon means 'stranger' in Greek; it powers bright car headlights and spacecraft ion engines.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Radon: Radon is a radioactive gas that seeps from soil into basements, and a leading cause of lung cancer in nonsmokers.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Bromine: Bromine is one of only two elements that are liquid at room temperature, a dark red-brown liquid that gives off fumes.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Mercury: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature, which is why old thermometers used it.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Sulfur: Sulfur is a yellow solid that smells of rotten eggs only when it forms hydrogen sulfide.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Carbon: Carbon is solid at room temperature in forms as different as soft graphite and diamond.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Iodine: Iodine is a solid that sublimes straight into violet vapor when heated.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Sodium: Sodium is a soft metal you can cut with a knife and it reacts explosively with water.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Phosphorus: White phosphorus is a waxy solid that glows faintly and can ignite in air, so it's stored underwater.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Boron: Boron is a hard solid, with a melting point above 2,000 degrees Celsius.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Lithium: Lithium is the lightest metal, light enough to float on oil, and a solid at room temperature.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Silicon: Silicon is a hard solid, the base of computer chips, and the second most abundant element in Earth's crust.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Calcium: Calcium is a soft solid metal, and the main mineral in bones and teeth.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Iron: Iron is a solid metal, and most of Earth's core is made of it.
Elements that are gases at room temperat.Gallium: Gallium melts at about 30 degrees Celsius, so it can turn to liquid in your hand, but it's solid at room temperature.

Physicists.Isaac Newton: His Principia of 1687 laid out the laws of motion and gravity, and he also ran the Royal Mint and hunted counterfeiters.
Physicists.Albert Einstein: He never won a Nobel for relativity; his 1921 prize was for explaining the photoelectric effect, which helped launch quantum theory.
Physicists.Niels Bohr: His 1913 atom model had electrons hopping between fixed orbits, and he later ran the Copenhagen institute that bears his name.
Physicists.Richard Feynman: He played bongo drums, cracked safes at Los Alamos, and won a Nobel for quantum electrodynamics. His lectures became a classic textbook.
Physicists.Marie Curie: The only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences, physics in 1903 and chemistry in 1911. Her notebooks are still radioactive.
Physicists.Max Planck: He founded quantum theory in 1900 by proposing that energy comes in tiny packets, which he reluctantly called quanta.
Physicists.Werner Heisenberg: His uncertainty principle says you can't know a particle's exact position and momentum together. He won the Nobel at just 31.
Physicists.Erwin Schrödinger: His famous cat thought experiment was meant to show how absurd he found the usual reading of quantum mechanics.
Physicists.Stephen Hawking: He held Newton's old Lucasian professorship at Cambridge and showed that black holes should slowly leak radiation.
Physicists.Galileo Galilei: He pointed an early telescope at Jupiter and spotted four moons circling it, evidence that not everything orbits Earth.
Physicists.Michael Faraday: A bookbinder's apprentice with little schooling, he discovered electromagnetic induction and gave the Royal Institution its Christmas lectures.
Physicists.James Clerk Maxwell: His four equations unified electricity, magnetism and light in the 1860s, and he took the first color photograph.
Physicists.Enrico Fermi: He built the first nuclear reactor under a Chicago football stadium in 1942. Element 100, fermium, is named for him.
Physicists.Paul Dirac: His equation of 1928 predicted antimatter before anyone had seen it, and the positron turned up a few years later.
Physicists.Charles Darwin: Darwin is a biologist, not a physicist. His 1859 book On the Origin of Species laid out evolution by natural selection.
Physicists.Gregor Mendel: Mendel was a monk who crossed pea plants and uncovered the basic rules of inheritance, but nobody noticed until after he died.
Physicists.Louis Pasteur: This chemist and microbiologist invented pasteurization and developed vaccines for rabies and anthrax, rather than doing physics.
Physicists.Sigmund Freud: Freud founded psychoanalysis in Vienna, so he belongs with psychology, not physics. He also wrote about dreams and the unconscious.
Physicists.Carl Linnaeus: The Swede who invented the system for naming species, with two Latin names each, including our own Homo sapiens. He was a botanist.
Physicists.Dmitri Mendeleev: He arranged the elements into a periodic table in 1869 and left gaps for undiscovered ones. He was a chemist, not a physicist.
Physicists.Alexander Fleming: A bacteriologist who noticed mold killing bacteria in 1928 and gave the world penicillin, which makes him a biologist.
Physicists.Jane Goodall: She spent decades studying wild chimpanzees at Gombe in Tanzania and found that they make and use tools. She's a primatologist.
Physicists.Antoine Lavoisier: The father of modern chemistry named oxygen and showed that matter is conserved in reactions. He was guillotined in 1794.
Physicists.Edward Jenner: He developed the smallpox vaccine in 1796 using cowpox, a doctor's breakthrough rather than a physicist's.

Missions to Mars.Viking 1: In 1976 it made the first successful Mars landing, and its robotic tests for life gave results scientists still debate.
Missions to Mars.Mariner 4: In 1965 it sent back the first close-up photos of Mars: 22 grainy images showing a cratered, Moon-like world.
Missions to Mars.Sojourner: The 1997 microwave-sized rover was the first to roll on Mars, and its Pathfinder lander made the landing with airbags.
Missions to Mars.Spirit: This rover landed in 2004 for a 90-day mission and kept going for about six years, partly because wind cleaned its solar panels.
Missions to Mars.Opportunity: Landed in 2004 for 90 days and lasted almost 15 years, until a global dust storm in 2018 silenced it, and found evidence of past water.
Missions to Mars.Curiosity: The car-sized rover has explored Gale Crater since 2012, landing with a sky crane, and it found that Mars once had conditions that could support life.
Missions to Mars.Perseverance: It landed in Jezero Crater in 2021 and is caching rock samples in tubes, which a future mission is meant to bring back to Earth.
Missions to Mars.Phoenix: In 2008 this lander dug into the north polar soil and confirmed water ice just below the surface.
Missions to Mars.InSight: A lander that placed the first seismometer on Mars in 2018 and recorded hundreds of marsquakes.
Missions to Mars.Mars Express: Europe's orbiter, at Mars since 2003, has probed below the surface with radar and mapped the planet in 3D with its stereo camera.
Missions to Mars.Zhurong: China's 2021 rover, named for a god of fire, landed on its first attempt on Mars, which very few missions manage.
Missions to Mars.Ingenuity: This small helicopter made the first powered flight on another planet in 2021, a test planned for 5 flights that made 72.
Missions to Mars.MAVEN: NASA's orbiter has studied the loss of Mars's atmosphere to space since 2014, helping explain how a wet world dried out.
Missions to Mars.Cassini: Launched in 2004, it studied Saturn and its moons for over a decade, not Mars.
Missions to Mars.Juno: This probe reached Jupiter in 2016 and studies its interior and auroras.
Missions to Mars.New Horizons: It was the first probe to fly past Pluto, in 2015, and it never went near Mars.
Missions to Mars.Voyager 2: Launched in 1977, it flew by Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, but not Mars.
Missions to Mars.Galileo: This probe orbited Jupiter and its moons from 1995 to 2003, and then was deliberately crashed into Jupiter.
Missions to Mars.Rosetta: The European probe landed on a comet in 2014, not Mars.
Missions to Mars.Huygens: The lander from Cassini touched down on Titan in 2005, which makes it the most distant landing ever.
Missions to Mars.Magellan: The 1990 radar mapper of Venus produced detailed maps through its thick clouds.
Missions to Mars.Dawn: The mission visited the asteroid Vesta and dwarf planet Ceres, using ion engines.
Missions to Mars.Hubble: The Space Telescope in orbit around Earth, which watches Mars but is not a mission to it.
Missions to Mars.Messenger: It was the first spacecraft to orbit Mercury, and it studied the planet from 2011 to 2015.

Hormones.Insulin: Discovered in 1921 by Banting and Best in Toronto, it let people with type 1 diabetes survive, and it was among the first hormones used as medicine.
Hormones.Adrenaline: Also called epinephrine, it triggers fight or flight within seconds, and it's the drug in an EpiPen for severe allergic reactions.
Hormones.Estrogen: The main female sex hormone, it shapes puberty and the menstrual cycle, and it also supports bone strength in both sexes.
Hormones.Testosterone: Produced mainly in the testes, it drives male puberty, and women make it in smaller amounts too.
Hormones.Cortisol: The stress hormone, which rises in the morning to help you wake up, and long-term high levels can harm sleep and immunity.
Hormones.Melatonin: Made in the pineal gland, it signals darkness to your body, and its release is suppressed by bright light at night.
Hormones.Thyroxine: Made by the thyroid gland, it regulates metabolism, and it needs iodine, which is why iodine deficiency causes goiter.
Hormones.Oxytocin: Sometimes called the cuddle hormone, it's released during childbirth, nursing and hugs, and it can strengthen social bonds.
Hormones.Growth hormone: Released by the pituitary gland, it drives growth in childhood, and its synthetic form is used in medicine and, controversially, in sport.
Hormones.Glucagon: Insulin's partner, made in the pancreas, it raises blood sugar by releasing stored glucose from the liver.
Hormones.Leptin: Made by fat cells, it tells the brain you've had enough to eat, and its name comes from the Greek word for thin.
Hormones.Hemoglobin: The protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen, and it's what makes blood red, but it isn't a hormone.
Hormones.Collagen: The most abundant protein in the body, it makes up skin, tendons and bones, and it's a structural protein, not a hormone.
Hormones.Keratin: The tough protein of hair, nails and horns, which is structural rather than a hormone.
Hormones.Pepsin: The enzyme that digests proteins in the stomach was among the first ever discovered, in 1836, and it's an enzyme, not a hormone.
Hormones.Amylase: An enzyme in saliva that starts breaking down starch, so a cracker tastes sweeter the longer you chew; it's an enzyme, not a hormone.
Hormones.Cholesterol: A waxy lipid that is a raw material for steroid hormones, but it isn't a hormone itself.
Hormones.Glucose: The sugar in your blood, and it's regulated by hormones, but it isn't one.
Hormones.Antibodies: Proteins your immune system makes to tag germs, which are not hormones even though they travel in blood.
Hormones.Plasma: The liquid part of blood, about 55 percent of it, carrying hormones, but not itself a hormone.
Hormones.Lactose: The sugar in milk, which many adults can't digest, and it isn't a hormone.
Hormones.Caffeine: A stimulant in coffee that blocks adenosine, a chemical that makes you sleepy, but it isn't a hormone.
Hormones.Penicillin: The first widely used antibiotic, a medicine from mold, and not something your body makes.
Hormones.Bile: Made in the liver and stored in the gallbladder, it helps digest fats, and it is a digestive fluid, not a hormone.

Steps of the scientific method.Observation: Science starts by noticing something puzzling, since even Newton's apple story is about an observation.
Steps of the scientific method.Question: A good question is specific and testable, like 'Does light affect plant growth?', and not 'Why is the world so strange?'
Steps of the scientific method.Research: Researching first shows what's already known, which prevents anyone from repeating work or making old errors.
Steps of the scientific method.Hypothesis: A hypothesis is a testable proposed explanation, and it must be possible to prove wrong, as Karl Popper pointed out.
Steps of the scientific method.Prediction: A prediction says what you should see if the hypothesis is true, which makes it testable.
Steps of the scientific method.Experiment: A fair experiment changes one variable at a time and keeps all else the same, so you can see the cause.
Steps of the scientific method.Data collection: Careful records, ideally numbers, let others check your work, and repeated measurements reduce the effect of chance.
Steps of the scientific method.Analysis: Analysis uses statistics to tell real effects from random noise, and it is where many surprising results are caught.
Steps of the scientific method.Conclusion: A conclusion states whether the data supported the hypothesis, and in science 'we were wrong' is a valid result.
Steps of the scientific method.Superstition: Superstition rests on belief without testing, so it can't be a step in the scientific method.
Steps of the scientific method.Rumor: A rumor spreads without evidence, but science needs testable evidence at every single step.
Steps of the scientific method.Prophecy: A prophecy claims to see the future by faith or vision, not by testing, so it is not a step in the scientific method.
Steps of the scientific method.Horoscope: A horoscope makes vague claims that fit anyone, and studies show astrology fails controlled tests.
Steps of the scientific method.Wishful thinking: Wishful thinking is believing what you want, and science tries to resist it using controls and blind tests.
Steps of the scientific method.Gut feeling: A gut feeling can inspire a hypothesis, but it is not evidence, and the method asks for tests.
Steps of the scientific method.Coin toss: A coin toss is random, and it doesn't test an idea, though scientists do use randomization in experiments.
Steps of the scientific method.Magic spell: A magic spell is not testable in science, and when tests are done, results come out no better than chance.
Steps of the scientific method.Tarot reading: Tarot reading depends on interpretation, not testing, so it is not part of the scientific method.
Steps of the scientific method.Blind faith: Blind faith means belief without evidence, which is the opposite of what the scientific method requires at each step.
Steps of the scientific method.Hearsay: Hearsay is a secondhand report, and science wants direct, checkable data, not what someone said they heard.
Steps of the scientific method.Gossip: Gossip spreads claims without checking, and a scientific method requires verification.
Steps of the scientific method.Ouija board: An Ouija board moves by tiny unconscious muscle movements, the ideomotor effect, so it is not a method of finding truth.
Steps of the scientific method.Fortune cookie: A fortune cookie, a snack with a slip of paper, has predictions that aren't tested, and the cookie is in fact an American Japanese-style invention.
Steps of the scientific method.Lucky charm: A lucky charm gives comfort but not evidence, and science cannot count it as a result.

Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Homo sapiens: That's us, meaning 'wise human' in Latin. The oldest known fossils are from Morocco, about 300,000 years old.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Homo erectus: This species lasted nearly two million years, longer than any other human relative, and was the first to spread widely out of Africa.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Homo habilis: The name means 'handy man' since its fossils were found with simple stone tools, around 2 million years old, in Tanzania.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Neanderthal: Neanderthals buried their dead and made tools. Many people today carry a few percent of their DNA from ancient interbreeding.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Australopithecus: Lucy, the famous 3.2-million-year-old skeleton found in Ethiopia in 1974, belonged to this genus and walked upright.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Denisovan: Known mostly from a finger bone and teeth in a Siberian cave, Denisovans were identified in 2010 through DNA alone.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Homo floresiensis: Nicknamed 'the hobbit', this tiny human stood about a meter tall and lived on the Indonesian island of Flores until roughly 50,000 years ago.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Homo naledi: Found in South Africa's Rising Star cave in 2013, it had a small brain but may have deliberately buried its dead, a controversial claim.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Ardipithecus: 'Ardi', a skeleton about 4.4 million years old from Ethiopia, showed that early hominins climbed trees and walked upright at once.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Paranthropus: Called 'nutcracker man', it had huge jaws and chewing muscles. Those let it grind tough plants, and it died out about a million years ago.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Homo heidelbergensis: This ancestor of both Neanderthals and possibly us lived about 600,000 years ago and may have built early shelters.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Gigantopithecus: This was a giant ape up to three meters tall that lived in Asia. It was an ape relative, not a hominin, and died out about 300,000 years ago.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Orangutan: Orangutans are great apes, so they're relatives but not hominins. Their name comes from Malay and means 'person of the forest'.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Gorilla: Gorillas share about 98 percent of our DNA, but they belong to a separate branch of the family, so they're not hominins.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Chimpanzee: Chimps are our closest living relatives, with about 98 percent shared DNA. They're not hominins because their line split off before humans.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Bigfoot: Bigfoot is a legend, with no fossil or DNA evidence. Hair samples tested over the years have turned out to be bears and other known animals.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Yeti: Himalayan legends of the Yeti were tested by DNA studies in 2017 that found hair and bone samples came from Asian bears.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Piltdown Man: This 1912 'missing link' in England was a hoax, exposed in 1953. It paired a medieval human skull with an orangutan jaw.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Lemur: Lemurs are primates found only on Madagascar, but are not hominins. They split from the ape line tens of millions of years ago.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Woolly mammoth: Mammoths were elephant relatives and lived alongside humans, who hunted them. They are not hominins and none survive.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Woolly rhino: Ice Age hunters painted this shaggy rhino in cave art. It's a relative of modern rhinos, not a human relative.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Megatherium: This giant ground sloth was as big as an elephant and lived in South America. Humans probably met it, but it's no relative of ours.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Baboon: Baboons are Old World monkeys with dog-like faces. They're primates but far more distant cousins than apes, and not hominins.
Hominins (humans and extinct relatives).Gibbon: Gibbons are small apes famed for swinging through trees and singing duets, but they branched off before the great apes, so they aren't hominins.

Animal sidekicks in Disney animated film.Heihei: Moana's Heihei is a rooster who seems brainless but keeps the plot moving by repeatedly swallowing the stone Heart of Te Fiti.
Animal sidekicks in Disney animated film.Sven: Kristoff speaks for his reindeer Sven. Reindeer are the only deer species in which both males and females grow antlers.
Animal sidekicks in Disney animated film.Pua: Moana's pet pig Pua reflects history, since Polynesian voyagers carried pigs aboard their canoes to settle new islands.
Animal sidekicks in Disney animated film.Maximus: Tangled's palace horse Maximus acts like a bloodhound on Flynn Rider's trail, yet never speaks a word.
Animal sidekicks in Disney animated film.Cri-Kee: Mulan's lucky cricket Cri-Kee reflects real tradition. In China, crickets are kept as pets for luck and for their song.
Animal sidekicks in Disney animated film.Donkey: Shrek's Donkey comes from DreamWorks, not Disney. Eddie Murphy voiced him, and also voiced Mushu at Disney.
Animal sidekicks in Disney animated film.Puss in Boots: Puss belongs to DreamWorks' Shrek films, not Disney. The original folk tale was published by Charles Perrault in 1697.

Animal sidekicks in Disney animated film.King Julien: King Julien is a ring-tailed lemur from DreamWorks' Madagascar, and real ring-tailed lemurs live only on that island.
Animal sidekicks in Disney animated film.Mort: Mort is a tiny mouse lemur from DreamWorks' Madagascar. Real mouse lemurs are among the smallest primates on Earth.
Animal sidekicks in Disney animated film.Toothless: Toothless, from DreamWorks' How to Train Your Dragon, is a Night Fury whose design borrows from black panthers and house cats.
Animal sidekicks in Disney animated film.Gizmo: Gizmo is the furry Mogwai from Warner Bros.' Gremlins, with rules: no water, no bright light, and never feed him after midnight.
Animal sidekicks in Disney animated film.Simba: Simba is the hero, not a sidekick. His name means 'lion' in Swahili.
Animal sidekicks in Disney animated film.Dumbo: Dumbo stars in his own 1941 film. The actual sidekick is Timothy Q. Mouse, his tiny ringmaster-style helper.
Animal sidekicks in Disney animated film.Bambi: Bambi is the hero of his own film, and Thumper the rabbit is the sidekick. Felix Salten wrote the novel in 1923.

Star Wars villains.Emperor Palpatine: Sheev Palpatine was both a Senator and the Sith Lord Darth Sidious. Ian McDiarmid first played him in 1983 and returned in 2019.
Star Wars villains.Darth Maul: He appears for under ten minutes in The Phantom Menace, yet his double-bladed lightsaber made him a fan favorite who later returned in animation.
Star Wars villains.Count Dooku: Christopher Lee played him in two prequels. Lee, who was a real-life swordsman and war veteran, did many of his own stunts.
Star Wars villains.Kylo Ren: Born Ben Solo, Han and Leia's son, he took his name from the Knights of Ren after being drawn to the dark side.
Star Wars villains.General Grievous: A cyborg with four arms who collects lightsabers from Jedi he has defeated. He coughs because his organic body is mostly replaced.
Star Wars villains.Grand Moff Tarkin: Peter Cushing played him in 1977 and was mocked for wearing slippers on set because the boots hurt. A digital version returned in Rogue One.
Star Wars villains.Jabba the Hutt: The crime lord of Tatooine was a huge puppet in Return of the Jedi, operated by several people, and the CGI version came in later releases.
Star Wars villains.Snoke: The First Order's Supreme Leader was played by Andy Serkis in motion capture, and he is killed off in The Last Jedi.
Star Wars villains.Captain Phasma: Gwendoline Christie played the chrome-armored stormtrooper commander. The role kept her face covered for nearly the whole film.
Star Wars villains.Thrawn: Grand Admiral Thrawn debuted in Timothy Zahn's 1991 novels, and later became canon, appearing in animation and the Ahsoka series.
Star Wars villains.General Hux: The ruthless First Order officer who gives a fiery speech in The Force Awakens was played by Domhnall Gleeson.
Star Wars villains.Asajj Ventress: She debuted in the animated Clone Wars as a Sith assassin, was originally Dooku's apprentice, and later turned bounty hunter.
Star Wars villains.Luke Skywalker: The hero, not a villain: he's the Jedi who nearly gave in to the dark side but refused to kill his father, which ultimately redeemed Vader.
Star Wars villains.Leia: Princess Leia is a Rebel leader and Luke's twin. Carrie Fisher's hair buns were inspired by Mexican revolutionary women, and are not villainous.
Star Wars villains.Han Solo: A smuggler turned rebel hero. His line 'I know' to Leia was improvised on set, and Harrison Ford suggested it in place of 'I love you too'.
Star Wars villains.Obi-Wan Kenobi: A Jedi master on the good side, though he does famously fall to Vader, who killed him in A New Hope.
Star Wars villains.Yoda: The Jedi master, not a villain. In the original films he was a puppet performed by Frank Oz, who also voiced Miss Piggy.
Star Wars villains.Mace Windu: A Jedi Council member played by Samuel L. Jackson, who requested a purple lightsaber so he would stand out in battle scenes.
Star Wars villains.Ahsoka: Anakin's former Padawan began in The Clone Wars. She is a hero who walked away from the Jedi Order, not a Sith.
Star Wars villains.Rey: The hero of the sequel trilogy. Despite the villain-like visions she sees, she chooses the light and is later revealed to be Palpatine's granddaughter.
Star Wars villains.Finn: A former stormtrooper who defects, and the first of the sequels' heroes we meet. He is known as FN-2187 in the Order.
Star Wars villains.Padme: Padme Amidala was queen then senator of Naboo, a heroine and mother to Luke and Leia, whose elaborate costumes are a famed feature of the prequels.
Star Wars villains.Qui-Gon Jinn: The Jedi master who discovers young Anakin, played by Liam Neeson. He is a hero who dies at Darth Maul's hands.

Words that go after 'sound'.Check: Before doors open, crews run a sound check, often repeating one song's chorus, so the engineer can set every level before the crowd arrives.
Words that go after 'sound'.Wave: Sound travels through air as pressure waves at about 343 metres per second, roughly 767 miles per hour at room temperature.
Words that go after 'sound'.Barrier: Chuck Yeager broke it in 1947 in the Bell X-1, and the sonic boom people hear is a shock wave, not a one-time bang.
Words that go after 'sound'.Track: The Jazz Singer in 1927 brought the first talkie, and a film's soundtrack mixes dialogue, music and effects on separate layers.
Words that go after 'sound'.System: Jamaican sound systems of the 1950s, with towering speakers in the street, inspired the DJ toasting that later became hip-hop.
Words that go after 'sound'.Proof: Egg cartons are a myth for soundproofing; real studios block noise with heavy mass, air gaps and rooms built within rooms.
Words that go after 'sound'.Bite: A sound bite is the short quote TV news picks from a speech, and the average one shrank to only seconds in modern US elections.
Words that go after 'sound'.Effect: Film Foley artists fake effects with everyday items: coconut halves for horse hooves, and celery snapped for breaking bones.
Words that go after 'sound'.Engineer: The person at the recording desk shapes how an album sounds. George Martin and Geoff Emerick helped craft the Beatles' studio innovations.
Words that go after 'sound'.Asleep: Here "sound" means deep and healthy, from an old word for whole, which also gives us "safe and sound" and "sound judgment".
Words that go after 'sound'.Mind: Of sound mind is a legal test, and a will can be challenged if the writer wasn't mentally competent when signing it.
Words that go after 'sound'.Card: The 1989 Sound Blaster card let ordinary PCs play music and effects instead of simple beeps, and it dominated 1990s gaming.
Words that go after 'sound'.Stage: A soundstage is a big soundproofed studio hall, and the Wizard of Oz's Yellow Brick Road was built on one at MGM.
Words that go after 'sound'.Pen: Sound pen is not a compound word in English, so nothing follows sound here, though a pen can scratch quite loudly.
Words that go after 'sound'.Cloud: "Sound cloud" is not a phrase on its own. SoundCloud, one word and a music-sharing site from Berlin, is the closest thing.
Words that go after 'sound'.Chair: Nobody says sound chair; a chair is furniture, though a famously creaky one can sound like it is complaining about your weight.
Words that go after 'sound'.Lamp: No such phrase as sound lamp exists in English; a lamp gives light, and a related phrase would be something like lamp shade.
Words that go after 'sound'.Shoe: There is no phrase sound shoe, though shoes, unlike lamps, make a lot of noise on a hard floor, so it is easy to imagine.
Words that go after 'sound'.Spoon: You can't say sound spoon in English, though tapping a spoon on a glass makes a famous ringing note, so the idea is not crazy.
Words that go after 'sound'.Tree: The old puzzle asks if a falling tree makes a sound with nobody around, but sound tree is not a compound phrase.
Words that go after 'sound'.Sock: Not a phrase: sound sock is nonsense, even if a thick sock really does muffle footsteps.
Words that go after 'sound'.Cake: Sound cake isn't a real expression, though a sponge cake and a sound sleep can both be the kind of thing you describe as solid.
Words that go after 'sound'.Banana: There is no phrase sound banana, though banana peels have a reputation in cartoons for sound effects when slipped on.
Words that go after 'sound'.Pillow: No such phrase as sound pillow exists; a pillow muffles noise, but it doesn't form a compound with sound.

NBA team nicknames.Steelers: A Pittsburgh NFL team, with six Super Bowl titles, named for the steel industry.
NBA team nicknames.Penguins: Pittsburgh's NHL team, with five Stanley Cup wins.
NBA team nicknames.Eagles: A Philadelphia NFL team that won Super Bowl LII and LIX, not in the NBA.
NBA team nicknames.Maple Leafs: Toronto's NHL team, whose Stanley Cup drought began in 1967.

Video game consoles.Nintendo Switch: The 2017 Switch is a hybrid: it docks to a TV or goes handheld, and has sold well over 100 million units.
Video game consoles.Wii: The Wii's motion controls brought non-gamers in, and its name was chosen because it sounds like the word 'we'.
Video game consoles.GameCube: Nintendo's 2001 cube-shaped console with a carrying handle used miniature discs rather than standard DVDs.
Video game consoles.Sega Genesis: In Japan and Europe it was called the Mega Drive; Sega Genesis was the North American name, chosen for legal reasons.
Video game consoles.Dreamcast: The 1998 Dreamcast was Sega's last console, and it had online play built in at a time when few consoles did.
Video game consoles.Game Boy: The 1989 Game Boy, bundled with Tetris, ran for ages on four AA batteries and outsold much flashier handhelds.
Video game consoles.Atari 2600: Launched in 1977, the 2600 is the console that made home video gaming mainstream, with its famous woodgrain panel.
Video game consoles.Nintendo 64: The 1996 Nintendo 64 had an unusual three-pronged controller and four controller ports built in.
Video game consoles.Steam Deck: Valve's 2022 handheld is basically a portable PC that plays Steam games, running a Linux-based system.
Video game consoles.PSP: Sony's 2004 PlayStation Portable used small optical discs called UMDs, which had a short life.
Video game consoles.Nintendo DS: The dual-screen DS from 2004 sold over 150 million units, making it one of the best-selling consoles ever.
Video game consoles.iPod: The iPod played music and some simple games, but it wasn't designed as a game console.
Video game consoles.Walkman: The Walkman is Sony's cassette player. It played music, not games.
Video game consoles.Tamagotchi: The Tamagotchi is a 1996 virtual pet on a keychain, popular but not a console.
Video game consoles.Kindle: Kindle is Amazon's e-reader and has no game console function.
Video game consoles.Roomba: A Roomba is a robot vacuum cleaner and has nothing to do with gaming.
Video game consoles.Fitbit: Fitbit makes fitness trackers worn on the wrist, not game systems.
Video game consoles.Discman: The Discman played CDs, like Sony's portable audio player.
Video game consoles.BlackBerry: BlackBerry phones had keyboards and a pre-smartphone cult following, but they weren't consoles.
Video game consoles.Furby: The 1998 Furby was a talking robot toy that learned words slowly. It was a toy, not a console.
Video game consoles.iPad: The iPad is a tablet that plays games, but it is not a dedicated game console.
Video game consoles.Chromecast: Chromecast is Google's streaming dongle that plugs into a TV; it isn't a console.
